extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patent practitioners, and patent examiners preparing or reviewing nucleotide/amino acid sequence listings for USPTO filings (WIPO ST.25 era)
extracted.subtask_description: Prepare and submit the "Sequence Listing" part of a patent application (nucleotide and/or amino acid sequences) in compliance with 37 CFR 1.821–1.825 and MPEP guidance implementing WIPO ST.25. Covers symbols, format, numeric identifiers, file-format requirements, and amendment procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on introduction of new matter when correcting sequences
rubrics_metrics.description: Corrections of errors in sequencing or any other errors made in describing an invention are subject to the statutory prohibition (35 U.S.C. 132 and 35 U.S.C. 251) against the introduction of new matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any amendment or correction adding sequence data must include a statement that the Sequence Listing includes no new matter and identify the basis in the original filing (see 37 CFR 1.825 requirements).

rubrics_metrics.name: Presumptions regarding compliance with sequence rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Neither the presence nor absence of information not required under the sequence rules creates a presumption that such information is necessary to satisfy 35 U.S.C. 112.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For applications subject to 37 CFR 1.821–1.825, the grant of a patent constitutes a presumption that the granted patent complies with these rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Symbols and format must conform to 37 CFR 1.822(b)-(e)
rubrics_metrics.description: The symbols and format used for nucleotide and/or amino acid sequence data shall conform to the requirements set forth in 37 CFR 1.822 paragraphs (b) through (e).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appendices A–F (to Subpart G) provide the code sets and feature keys; no other symbols shall be used in sequence listings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Character code set requirement (Appendices A and C)
rubrics_metrics.description: The code for representing nucleotide and amino acid sequence characters must conform to the code set forth in appendices A and C; no other code may be used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Modified bases or unusual amino acids listed in Appendices B and D may be presented as the corresponding unmodified symbol only if the modification is set forth in the Feature section. Otherwise, use 'n' or 'Xaa' and provide further information in the Feature section using keys from Appendices E and F.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nucleotide one-letter symbol convention and case
rubrics_metrics.description: Nucleotide sequences shall be listed using the lowercase letter for representing the one-letter code for the nucleotide bases set forth in Appendix A.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not use other symbols; modified/unknown bases handled as in the code-set requirement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grouping of nucleotide bases in noncoding and coding regions
rubrics_metrics.description: Bases in a nucleotide sequence (including introns) shall be listed in groups of 10 bases except in coding parts; leftover fewer-than-10 bases at the end of noncoding parts shall be grouped together and separated by a space.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide spaces between adjacent groups of 10 or 3 bases per the formatting rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coding parts must be shown as codons with amino acids beneath
rubrics_metrics.description: Bases in coding parts shall be listed as triplets (codons) and the amino acids corresponding to those codons shall be listed immediately below the corresponding codons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a codon spans an intron, the amino acid symbol shall be listed below the portion of the codon containing two nucleotides.

rubrics_metrics.name: Line length limits for nucleotide sequences
rubrics_metrics.description: A nucleotide sequence shall be listed with a maximum of 16 codons or 60 bases per line, with a space provided between each codon or group of 10 bases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This formatting standard governs presentation in the Sequence Listing; other line-length limits (e.g., ASCII/PDF file constraints) also apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Single-strand representation and directionality
rubrics_metrics.description: A nucleotide sequence shall be represented only by a single strand, in the 5' to 3' direction, from left to right.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not represent double-stranded nucleotides as duplexes in the Sequence Listing; double-stranded molecules may be represented as two single strands and relationships shown in drawings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enumeration of nucleotide bases
rubrics_metrics.description: Enumeration of nucleotide bases shall start at the first base of the sequence with number 1 and be continuous through the sequence in the 5' to 3' direction. Enumeration shall appear in the right margin next to the line showing the number of the last base on that line.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For circular sequences the enumeration method remains applicable but the designation of the first base may be chosen at the applicant's option.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amino acid three-letter code and case
rubrics_metrics.description: Amino acids in protein or peptide sequences shall be listed using three-letter abbreviations with the first letter uppercase and the remaining two letters lowercase (e.g., Ala) as in Appendix C.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants are encouraged to use three-letter symbols throughout the disclosure for readability instead of one-letter symbols.

rubrics_metrics.name: Line length and spacing for amino acid sequences
rubrics_metrics.description: A protein or peptide sequence shall be listed with a maximum of 16 amino acids per line with a space provided between each amino acid.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amino acid sequences are represented amino- to carboxy-direction left-to-right; amino/carboxy groups are not represented.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amino acid enumeration alternatives
rubrics_metrics.description: Amino acid sequences may be numbered starting with the first amino acid of the first mature protein as 1 (with preceding residues numbered negatively) or starting at the amino terminal as number 1; when used, enumeration should appear below every five amino acids.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choice of numbering method is permitted; for circular amino acid sequences the designation of first amino acid may be at applicant's option.

rubrics_metrics.name: Internal terminator symbols require separate sequences
rubrics_metrics.description: An amino acid sequence that contains internal terminator symbols (e.g., 'Ter', '*', '.') may not be represented as a single amino acid sequence and must be represented as separate amino acid sequences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Split into separate sequences when terminator symbols are internal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gapped and noncontiguous sequences representation
rubrics_metrics.description: A sequence with a gap or gaps shall be represented as multiple separate sequences, each with a separate sequence identifier; the number of sequences equals the number of continuous strings of sequence data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gaps mean unknown or undisclosed regions between known/disclosed regions. However, a sequence that contains regions of contiguous 'n' or 'Xaa' with the exact number disclosed may be included as a single sequence; fragments of larger sequences can be referred to by residue range without being enumerated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of Feature section for modified/unknown residues
rubrics_metrics.description: If 'n', 'Xaa', or a modified/unusual L-amino acid or modified base is used, the Feature section (<220>–<223>) must include further information and appropriate feature keys from Appendices E and F.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Modified bases/amino acids listed in Appendices B/D may be shown as unmodified symbols only if the modification is also detailed in the Feature section.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sequence Listing content order and numeric identifiers (Appendix G)
rubrics_metrics.description: The order and presentation of items in the Sequence Listing must conform to Appendix G; each item begins on a new line with the numeric identifier enclosed in angle brackets and mandatory ('M') items must be submitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Numeric identifiers <110> through <170> must appear at the beginning. See Appendix G for required/optional fields and formats.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include each disclosed nucleotide and/or amino acid sequence
rubrics_metrics.description: The Sequence Listing must include each disclosed nucleotide and/or amino acid sequence as defined in 37 CFR 1.821(a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Every sequence meeting the statutory/ regulatory definition must be present (or indicated by code '000' if no sequence is present for a sequence identifier).

rubrics_metrics.name: Separate SEQ ID NO for each sequence and sequencing of identifiers
rubrics_metrics.description: Assign a separate sequence identifier (SEQ ID NO) to each sequence beginning with 1 and increase sequentially by integers; include the sequence identifier in numeric identifier <210>.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use code '000' in place of the sequence where no sequence is present for a sequence identifier.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include total number of SEQ ID NOs (<160>)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Sequence Listing must include the total count of SEQ ID NOs in numeric identifier <160> whether followed by a sequence or by the code '000'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure the total reflects all sequence identifiers present in the listing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Line and page character limits for Sequence Listing submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: Sequence Listing submissions must not contain more than 74 characters per line. For PDF/printed Sequence Listings, sheets should contain no more than 66 lines with each line no more than 74 characters and should use a fixed-width font.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PDF Sequence Listing must begin on a new page and be titled 'Sequence Listing' and must not include material other than the Sequence Listing itself.

rubrics_metrics.name: ASCII plain text submission incorporation-by-reference requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Sequence Listing is submitted as an ASCII plain text file via the USPTO electronic filing system or on a read-only optical disc, the specification must contain a separate paragraph incorporating by reference the ASCII file identifying the file name, creation date, and file size (except for international applications during the international stage).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the format specified in 37 CFR 1.77(b)(5) for the incorporation paragraph.

rubrics_metrics.name: ASCII plain text file format and character requirements (37 CFR 1.824)
rubrics_metrics.description: ASCII plain text files must be PC or Mac compatible and in ASCII plain text; all printable characters permitted; no nonprintable ASCII control characters except CRLF or LF line terminators.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filename must be *.txt (<=60 characters excluding extension), only letters, numbers, hyphens, underscores; no spaces; file must be one continuous file (no hard page breaks or pagination) and no more than 74 printable characters per line.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission media, size, and compression rules for ASCII files
rubrics_metrics.description: An ASCII Sequence Listing may be submitted electronically via the USPTO filing system where the file must not exceed 100 MB and compression is not permitted; or on read-only optical disc(s) in compliance with 37 CFR 1.52(e) where compression (WinZip, 7-Zip, Unix Zip) is allowed subject to restrictions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compressed files must not be self-extracting; large compressed files may be split for disc storage per disc size and labeling rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: PDF/physical Sequence Listing formatting rules (37 CFR 1.823(b)(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: A Sequence Listing submitted as a PDF or on physical sheets must: begin on a new page; be titled 'Sequence Listing'; include only the Sequence Listing; have no more than 66 lines per sheet and no more than 74 characters per line; sheets should be independently numbered at the beginning; and should use a fixed-width font exclusively.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If submitted as PDF/physical sheets and a separate CRF is required, include the CRF and ensure consistency between CRF and Sequence Listing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appendix G numeric identifiers and required fields (examples)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the numeric identifiers specified in Appendix G (<110>–<170>, <210>, <211>, <212>, <213>, <220>–<223>, etc.) with specified formats and mandatory/optional status for each item (e.g., <210> SEQ ID NO, <211> Length, <212> Type, <213> Organism, <220> Feature, <160> Number of SEQ ID NOs).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some fields are mandatory only under certain conditions (e.g., <220>–<223> are mandatory if 'n', 'Xaa', modified residues are used or organism is 'Artificial'/'Unknown'); see Appendix G for exact conditions and required formats (dates, identifiers, integer formats, organism names).

rubrics_metrics.name: Informational requirements for Sequence Listing content
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 CFR 1.823(a) requires specific content including sequence identifiers, item order per Appendix G, mandatory vs optional items, line spacing, and numeric identifiers; numeric identifiers <110>–<170> must be at the start of the Sequence Listing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP § 2431 for a sample Sequence Listing and MPEP § 2422.03 discussion of 37 CFR 1.821(c).

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendment requirements when adding a Sequence Listing after filing (37 CFR 1.825(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: Any amendment adding a Sequence Listing after the application filing date must include: the Sequence Listing in an accepted format (ASCII file, PDF, or paper); a request that the amendment be made (by incorporation for ASCII or by inserting after the abstract for PDF/paper); a statement identifying the basis in the original filing for all sequence data; a statement that the Sequence Listing includes no new matter; a new or substitute CRF if required; and a statement that CRF sequence information matches the added Sequence Listing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If ASCII plain text is used as both Sequence Listing and CRF, an incorporation-by-reference paragraph is required in the specification (except for international applications during the international stage).

rubrics_metrics.name: Replacement Sequence Listing requirements (37 CFR 1.825(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: A replacement Sequence Listing must be submitted in an accepted format and labeled 'REPLACEMENT MM/DD/YYYY' for ASCII files; must include a request for amendment (by incorporation for ASCII or placement after abstract for PDF/paper), identify locations of deletions/replacements/additions, indicate basis in the original filing for amended data, state that replacement includes no new matter, provide new/substitute CRF when needed, and state that CRF data matches the replacement Sequence Listing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the same format and CRF consistency requirements as for adding a Sequence Listing; replacements require explicit identification of changes and basis references.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specification amendment when ASCII Sequence Listing filed without incorporation
rubrics_metrics.description: If the complete application's specification was filed with an ASCII Sequence Listing but without incorporation-by-reference of the ASCII file, the specification must be amended to include a separate paragraph incorporating the ASCII file (except for international/national stage international applications).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This amendment replaces any prior incorporation paragraph as applicable and is required to maintain the ASCII file as part of the specification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-issue amendments to Sequence Listing must comply with replacement rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Any amendments to the Sequence Listing in a patent (e.g., reissue, reexamination, certificate of correction) must comply with the replacement Sequence Listing requirements set forth in 37 CFR 1.825(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat post-issue Sequence Listing changes the same as replacement Sequence Listings with statements about basis, no new matter, CRF, and identification of changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Citation and patent-document identification guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Throughout 37 CFR 1.823(a) and MPEP, patent documents and publications referenced in Sequence Listing items should be identified using WIPO standards (country code, number, filing date, kind code) and proper citation formats for PCT and WO documents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use WIPO ST.3 Annex A for country codes and WIPO ST.16 for kind codes; contact Office of International Patent Legal Administration for citation questions. Proper formatting aids interoperability and clarity in Sequence Listing items (e.g., publication/patent citation fields).
